title: Dynamic kernel packing telemetry and attention-stall detector
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Add lightweight runtime telemetry and detectors to measure effectiveness of dynamic kernel packing and to surface attention-related stalls during prefill/decode. The goal is to produce actionable per-request signals (pack efficiency, inter-kernel wait time, attention stall ratio) that feed Console dashboards, rollout gating, and automated tuning suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
acceptance_criteria: New NVTX ranges emitted for pack:start / pack:end and pack:kernel:<name> are present in traces and can be correlated to GPU kernels in perf exporter.
Per-request metrics exported: pack_efficiency (0-1), kernel_queue_wait_ms (p50/p95), attention_stall_ratio (0-1).
Console shows heatmap of pack_efficiency by model and sequence length bucket and an attention-stall scatter for requests with tail latency > SLA.
Integration test validates that instrumentation has <= 1% added CPU overhead and NVTX insertion cost does not materially impact p50 latency on microbench harness.
Alert rule created: attention_stall_ratio > 0.25 for > 5% of requests in 10m window triggers paging for SRE runbook.
Telemetry dataset documented and a migration guide for existing dashboards provided.
tasks: Design NVTX naming and span tags for pack boundaries and per-kernel attribution (owner: Marco).
Implement pack instrumentation in scheduler packer: emit pack:start/pack:end and per-kernel markers (owner: Marco + runtime team).
Compute pack_efficiency in runtime (tokens_in_packed_batch / ideal_tokens) and attach as request attribute (owner: infra-metrics).
Implement attention_stall_detector: compare decode prefills KV-cache hit patterns and kernel idle gaps to produce attention_stall_ratio (owner: Aisha).
Add exporter hooks to send metrics to telemetry pipeline with tags: model, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, route, deployment_type (owner: metrics).
Create Console visualizations (heatmap, scatter, percentile line) and an alert (owner: Console PM).
Benchmark and compare baseline vs packed instrumentation across seq_len [8,32,128,512] and batch sizes; publish results (owner: perf-team).
notes: Trade-offs: NVTX insertion increases trace fidelity but may add tiny CPU overhead; we will gate full resolution NVTX with a runtime sampling rate (default 1%).
Decision: use succinct NVTX keys to keep envelope size small: pack:start, pack:end, pack:kernel:<short_name>. We will map short_name->full metadata in exporter lookup to avoid large NVTX payloads.

Observation from prototype runs: dynamic packing improved throughput for short sequences but introduced occasional kernel queueing spikes when mixed seq lengths are present. Instrumentation should capture this spike pattern and label it as 'pack-mismatch'.

We evaluated two attention-stall heuristics: (A) inter-kernel idle > threshold; (B) KV cache miss ratio correlated with decode stalls. We will emit both signals and synthesize an attention_stall_ratio combining them with tunable weights.
Privacy: no request-level text is exported. All telemetry uses hashed request_id and aggregated buckets for Console.
